prerequisites: Knowledge of differential and integral calculus of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering related to: complex variable, integral calculus in several variables and differential equations.
Basic knowledge of computer programs with application in engineering.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, which enables students to learn new methods and technologies, as well as providing versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Industrial Technical Engineer's activity.
Propose and calculate integrals of functions of two and three variables and apply them to solving engineering problems.
Parametrize curves and surfaces fluently, perform integration of scalar and vector functions over them, and apply this to solving engineering problems.
Understand the basic properties of complex functions and be able to approximate them through series expansions.
Understand the essential qualitative aspects of differential equations: existence, uniqueness and regularity of solutions.
Acquire proficiency in the explicit resolution of first-order and higher-order differential equations and relate the latter to first-order systems.
Understand the concept of partial differential equation.

syllabus_topics: Teoremas de Green, Stokes y Gauss.
Integración compleja. Teorema de los residuos.
Introducción a las ecuaciones diferenciales ordinarias.
teaching_methods: Use of virtual campus for activities and providing information and teaching materials
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination: The final grade (NF) is calculated as 0.15*NL + 0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, where NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, and NC is the average of the two written partial controls. If a student does not achieve a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 in NC, the final grade will be a failing grade, and the numerical grade on the transcript will be the minimum of NF and 4. Students who do not attend the ordinary examination will be marked as 'No presentado'. For extraordinary examination: The final grade (NF) is 0.15*NL + max{0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC}, where NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, and NC is the exam grade. If a student does not achieve a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 in NC, the final grade will be a failing grade, and the numerical grade on the transcript will be the minimum of NF and 4. Students requesting differentiated evaluation will be assessed by a theoretical exam (85% weight) and a practical exam (15% weight).
